mission:
Add a text utility module to this library as ONE task (do not split it into several tasks): src/text.js with node:test tests in test/text.test.js.
It exports four functions, each with its own tests. In wrap, truncate and countWords a word is a maximal run of non-whitespace characters.
1. `slugify(text)`: lower-case, strip diacritics (NFD), replace every run of characters other than a-z and 0-9 with a single "-", trim "-" from both ends; throws TypeError when the argument is not a string.
2. `wrap(text, width)`: greedy word wrap into lines of at most `width` characters, a word longer than the width alone on its line; returns the lines joined with a line feed; throws TypeError unless width is a positive integer.
3. `truncate(text, max)`: returns the text unchanged when it fits; otherwise the longest prefix of whole words that fits in `max - 1` characters followed by "…" (when not even the first word fits: its first `max - 1` characters followed by "…").
4. `countWords(text)`: the number of words; 0 for an empty or all-whitespace string.
Record one design decision with the decision tool stating that word definition. `npm test` must pass. Commit as you see fit.

assumptions: The module is not re-exported from `src/index.js`; the request asks only for `src/text.js` and its test file, so `src/index.js`, `package.json` and `README.md` stay untouched.

`wrap` splits the text into words on whitespace and joins the words on a line with a single space, so original whitespace runs and newlines are not preserved; a line's length counts those single spaces. An empty or all-whitespace text gives an empty string.

`truncate` measures 'fits' as `text.length <= max` (UTF-16 code units, like `String.prototype.length`). The whole-word prefix is a prefix of the original text ending at the end of a word, with original internal whitespace kept and no trailing whitespace before the "…".
`truncate` and `countWords` add no argument validation, because the request specifies TypeErrors only for `slugify` (non-string) and `wrap` (width not a positive integer).
In `slugify`, combining marks left after NFD normalisation are removed so that 'é' becomes 'e' instead of producing a '-'.
The worker role has access to `mcp__nexus__record_decision`; the planner deliberately does not record the decision, so that exactly one is recorded.
The worker makes one commit on the current branch (`main`) containing only the two new files; the request leaves commit structure open.

tasks.title: Add src/text.js (slugify, wrap, truncate, countWords) with node:test tests
tasks.description:
Repository: a tiny dependency-free ESM package `textkit` (`package.json` has `"type": "module"` and `"test": "node --test"`; Node v24). Existing files are `src/index.js` (`export const VERSION = '1.0.0'`) and `test/index.test.js`, which uses `import test from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`, single quotes, no semicolons and one-line tests. Match that style. Environment is native Windows; do not rely on POSIX tools.

Create `src/text.js` with four named exports and create `test/text.test.js` with node:test tests for each function. Do not modify `src/index.js`, `package.json`, `README.md` or `test/index.test.js`. Add no dependencies.

Word definition (used by wrap, truncate and countWords): a word is a maximal run of non-whitespace characters (i.e. `/\S+/g` matches).

1. `slugify(text)`: throw `TypeError` if `text` is not a string. Otherwise lower-case it, normalise with NFD and strip the combining diacritic marks (so 'é' becomes 'e'), replace every run of characters other than a-z and 0-9 with a single '-', and trim '-' from both ends. Example: `'  Crème Brûlée!! 2024 '` gives `'creme-brulee-2024'`; `''` and `'!!!'` give `''`.

2. `wrap(text, width)`: throw `TypeError` unless `width` is a positive integer (reject 0, negatives, non-integers such as 2.5, NaN, and non-numbers such as '10'). Greedy word wrap: take the words in order and add each to the current line, separated by a single space, as long as the line stays at most `width` characters; otherwise start a new line. A word longer than `width` goes alone on its own line, unsplit. Return the lines joined with '\n'. Empty or all-whitespace text returns `''`.

3. `truncate(text, max)`: if `text.length <= max`, return `text` unchanged. Otherwise return the longest prefix of the text that ends at the end of a whole word and is at most `max - 1` characters long, followed by '…' (U+2026), with no trailing whitespace before the ellipsis. If not even the first word fits in `max - 1` characters, return the first `max - 1` characters of that word followed by '…'. Examples: `truncate('hello world foo', 12)` gives `'hello world…'`; `truncate('hello world', 8)` gives `'hello…'`; `truncate('abcdefghij', 5)` gives `'abcd…'`; `truncate('hello', 5)` gives `'hello'`.

4. `countWords(text)`: return the number of words; 0 for an empty or all-whitespace string. Runs of mixed whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines) count as one separator.

Tests in `test/text.test.js` must cover, per function: normal cases, the edge cases above, and the TypeError cases for `slugify` and `wrap` (use `assert.throws(..., TypeError)`). For `wrap`, include an exact-fit line, a word longer than the width, and multiple-whitespace input. For `truncate`, include text that fits exactly, a whole-word cut, and the first-word-too-long case. Write the implementation to the specification, not to the tests; do not weaken or skip tests to get a pass.

Record exactly ONE design decision with `mcp__nexus__record_decision` stating the word definition: in wrap, truncate and countWords a word is a maximal run of non-whitespace characters, with a short rationale (one shared definition keeps the three functions consistent). Do not record any other decision.

Run `npm test` and confirm that all tests pass, including the existing `version` test. Then commit only the two new files on the current branch with a concise message, ending the commit message with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Do not push. Leave no temporary files behind.
acceptanceCriteria: `src/text.js` exports the named functions `slugify`, `wrap`, `truncate` and `countWords` as ESM exports.
`slugify('  Crème Brûlée!! 2024 ')` returns `'creme-brulee-2024'`, and `slugify(42)` throws TypeError.
`wrap('the quick brown fox', 10)` returns `'the quick\nbrown fox'`; a word longer than the width sits alone on its line; `wrap('a', 0)`, `wrap('a', 2.5)` and `wrap('a', '10')` throw TypeError.
`truncate('hello', 5)` returns `'hello'`; `truncate('hello world foo', 12)` returns `'hello world…'`; `truncate('abcdefghij', 5)` returns `'abcd…'`.
`test/text.test.js` contains node:test tests for each of the four functions, and `npm test` exits 0 with every test passing, including the existing `version` test.
Exactly one decision is recorded via `mcp__nexus__record_decision`, stating that a word is a maximal run of non-whitespace characters in wrap, truncate and countWords.
The changes are committed; `git status` is clean and `git diff --stat 8385f6d HEAD` lists only `src/text.js` and `test/text.test.js`.

risks.description: The request leaves some `truncate` and `wrap` details open: whether whitespace inside the kept prefix is preserved, what happens with leading whitespace, and what an invalid `max` does. An implementation and a verifier could read these differently.
risks.mitigation: The assumptions and the task description fix one interpretation with concrete input/output examples, and the tests encode those examples.

risks.description: `slugify` could turn accented letters into '-' if combining marks are not removed after NFD normalisation.
risks.mitigation: The task requires stripping the combining marks and includes an accented-input acceptance example ('Crème Brûlée').

risks.description: The '…' character (U+2026) could be mis-encoded if the files are written through a Windows shell using a non-UTF-8 codepage, which would make the tests fail or pass incorrectly.
risks.mitigation: Write the files as UTF-8 with the file-writing tool rather than shell redirection, or use the `'…'` escape in source and tests.

risks.description: The decision could be recorded more than once (for example on a retry), breaking the 'one design decision' requirement.
risks.mitigation: The planner records no decision, and the task says to record exactly one; on a retry the worker should not record it again if it already has.

decisions.title: Shared word definition
decisions.decision: In wrap, truncate and countWords a word is a maximal run of non-whitespace characters (/\S+/g matches).
